cited_by.title: Hair breakage, growth and keeping length

record.population: 30 women (15 frequent braiders against 15 comparison women); hair fibres studied in the laboratory
record.design: Fibre damage after standardised combing strokes and comparison of braiders and non-braiders
record.finding: Cuticle damage rose in a linear trend with the number of combing strokes; 480 strokes did more cuticle damage than frequent braiding. Frequent braiders had weaker, thinner fibres.
record.note: Small. Funder not stated in the abstract. Hair-fibre measurements, not hair length kept.
